summary: VERDICT: PASS (investigation complete, finding confirmed). (1) billing-enforcement.guard.ts (apps/api/src/core/guards/billing-enforcement.guard.ts): independently probed route casing, trailing-slash, and dot-segment/percent-encoded path-traversal bypasses against normalizePath/startsWithAny using a live Express harness matching this repo's express version. Confirmed empirically: Express never resolves .. segments or decodes %2f for route matching (all traversal payloads 404, never reach a controller), and case-insensitive routing only ever makes the guard MORE restrictive (differently-cased originalUrl fails the case-sensitive ALWAYS_ALLOWED_PREFIXES match and falls through to deny), never less. Guard order (RateLimitGuard -> JwtAuthGuard -> MustChangePasswordGuard -> TenantGuard -> BillingEnforcementGuard) guarantees request.tenant is always a valid non-empty id or the request already threw before reaching this guard, so the tenantId.length===0 fail-open branch is not reachable for protected routes. No bypass found; the blanket-deny-except-allowlist rework is a fail-safe improvement over the prior enumerated denylist. No finding filed for this file. (2) leads.service.ts:326 (find-a22e0dad, HIGH): confirmed as a live, reproducible regression, not hypothetical -- ran leads.service.spec.ts, test 'a checagem de billing deveria bloquear o tenant suspenso' FAILS (promise resolves instead of rejecting). Root cause verified by reading billing.service.ts:328-341 (P0-A-R3/R4 comment) and leads.service.spec.ts:159-183: this session correctly stopped deriving tenants.active from tenant_billing_state.status (that conflation was itself a prior bug), but leads.service.ts's public unauthenticated submitPublicArtistApplication path (getPublicWorkspaceBySlug line 326) still gates only on tenants.active/deleted_at/allow_public_registration and has zero dependency on BillingEnforcementService, so a suspended tenant's public lead-capture form keeps working indefinitely. Traced downstream impact: emits DOMAIN_EVENTS.LEAD_CREATED, consumed by workflow-automation.service.ts and crm-followup.automation.ts -- real automation runs for a non-paying tenant, not just an inert DB write. Severity assessment: HIGH is correct and is NOT softened. This is a genuine authorization/business-rule bypass of the billing paywall boundary at a real unauthenticated entry point (BillingEnforcementGuard structurally cannot cover it, since the route is @Public()), but it is bounded to one write-only public intake endpoint with no cross-tenant data exposure and no privilege escalation into existing protected resources, which is why it stays HIGH rather than CRITICAL. Independently re-derived and filed as find-f10e1fcf (superseding taxonomy has no DUPLICATE disposition value; tracked as a corroborating twin of find-a22e0dad rather than merged) with the added automation-fanout evidence and the concrete failing-test proof. Recommended fix (not implemented, read-only review): getPublicWorkspaceBySlug / submitPublicArtistApplication must additionally consult tenant_billing_state.status (BillingEnforcementService.getState) and reject when suspended/read_only.
